parts.problem_md:
A curve is given by `y equals ln open parentheses 1 plus x to the power of 4 close parentheses`.

Use calculus to find the approximate change in $y$ as $x$ increases from $-1$ to $-1+k$ where $k$ is small.
parts.solution_md:
> *In general, the approximate change in *$y$* as *$x$* increases from *$a$* to *$a+h$* where *$h$* is small is *$\frac{dy}{dx}\timesh$* where *$\frac{dy}{dx}$* is at *$x=a$

> *Substitute *$a=-1$* and *$h=k$* into the expression above*

$\frac{dy}{dx}\timesk$* where *$\frac{dy}{dx}$* is at *$x=-1$

> *Find *$\frac{dy}{dx}$* using the chain rule, *$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{dy}{du}\frac{du}{dx}$* where *$u=1+x^{4}$

`table row y equals cell ln space u space space space space space space space space space space u equals 1 plus x to the power of 4 end cell row cell fraction numerator straight d y over denominator straight d u end fraction end cell equals cell 1 over u space space space space space space space space space space space fraction numerator straight d u over denominator straight d x end fraction equals 4 x cubed end cell end table`

> *This gives*

`table row cell fraction numerator straight d y over denominator straight d x end fraction end cell equals cell 1 over u cross times 4 x cubed end cell row blank equals cell fraction numerator 1 over denominator 1 plus x to the power of 4 end fraction cross times 4 x cubed end cell row blank equals cell fraction numerator 4 x cubed over denominator 1 plus x to the power of 4 end fraction end cell end table`

**[M1 A1]**

> *Substitute *$x=-1$* into *$\frac{dy}{dx}$

`table row cell fraction numerator straight d y over denominator straight d x end fraction end cell equals cell fraction numerator 4 open parentheses negative 1 close parentheses cubed over denominator 1 plus open parentheses negative 1 close parentheses to the power of 4 end fraction equals negative 2 end cell end table`

**[M1]**

> *Substitute *`table row blank blank cell fraction numerator straight d y over denominator straight d x end fraction end cell end table equals negative 2`* into *$\frac{dy}{dx}\timesk$

$-2k$

parts.problem_md:
A sector from a circle of radius $r$ has an internal angle of $θ$ radians, as shown below.

![Diagram of a sector with radius r, central angle θ radians, and the arc forming a part of a circle. Lines are marked to indicate the radius.](assets/001-diagram-of-a-sector-with-radius-r-central-angle-.png)

The perimeter of the sector is 4 units and the area of the sector is $A$ square units.

Show that `A equals fraction numerator 8 theta over denominator open parentheses 2 plus theta close parentheses squared end fraction`.
parts.solution_md:
> *The formula for the length of the arc in radians is *$rθ$

> *Find an expression for the total perimeter and set it equal to 4*

`table row cell r plus r theta plus r end cell equals 4 row cell 2 r plus r theta end cell equals cell 4 space space space space space space space space space space circle enclose 1 end cell end table`

**[B1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> This mark is for any correct perimeter equation that uses 4 and $rθ$.

> *The formula for the area of the arc in radians is *$\frac{1}{2}r^{2}θ$

> *Find an expression for the area *$A$

`A equals 1 half r squared theta table row blank blank space end table table row blank blank space end table table row blank blank space end table table row blank blank space end table table row blank blank space end table table row blank blank space end table table row blank blank space end table table row blank blank space end table table row blank blank space end table table row blank blank space end table table row blank blank cell circle enclose 2 end cell end table`

> *Eliminate *$r$*, e.g. make *$r$* the subject of equation 1 by first factorising it out*

`table row cell r open parentheses 2 plus theta close parentheses end cell equals 4 row r equals cell fraction numerator 4 over denominator 2 plus theta end fraction end cell end table`

**[M1]**

> *Then substitute this into equation 2*

`A equals 1 half open parentheses fraction numerator 4 over denominator 2 plus theta end fraction close parentheses squared cross times theta`

> *i.e. substitute *$y=e^{u}$* and *$u=4x-x^{2}$* into *$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{dy}{du}\times\frac{du}{dx}$

`fraction numerator straight d y over denominator straight d x end fraction equals straight e to the power of u cross times open parentheses 4 minus 2 x close parentheses`

Show that the second derivative of the curve `y equals straight e to the power of open parentheses 4 x minus x squared close parentheses end exponent` satisfies the relationship

`fraction numerator straight d squared y over denominator straight d x squared end fraction equals open parentheses p plus q x plus r x squared close parentheses y`

parts.solution_md:
> *Differentiate *`fraction numerator straight d y over denominator straight d x end fraction equals 2 open parentheses 2 minus x close parentheses straight e to the power of open parentheses 4 x minus x squared close parentheses end exponent`* again to get *$\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}$* but this time using the product rule *$\frac{du}{dx}v+u\frac{dv}{dx}$

> *First find the derivatives of *`u equals 2 open parentheses 2 minus x close parentheses equals 4 minus 2 x`* and *`v equals straight e to the power of open parentheses 4 x minus x squared close parentheses end exponent`*  (note that *$\frac{dv}{dx}$*is the answer to part (a))*

`fraction numerator straight d u over denominator straight d x end fraction equals negative 2
fraction numerator straight d v over denominator straight d x end fraction equals 2 open parentheses 2 minus x close parentheses straight e to the power of open parentheses 4 x minus x squared close parentheses end exponent`

> *Then substitute these into *$\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}=\frac{du}{dx}v+u\frac{dv}{dx}$

`fraction numerator straight d squared y over denominator straight d x squared end fraction equals open parentheses negative 2 close parentheses cross times straight e to the power of open parentheses 4 x minus x squared close parentheses end exponent plus open parentheses 4 minus 2 x close parentheses cross times open square brackets 2 open parentheses 2 minus x close parentheses straight e to the power of open parentheses 4 x minus x squared close parentheses end exponent close square brackets`

> *Simplify*

> *Factorise out *`straight e to the power of open parentheses 4 x minus x squared close parentheses end exponent`* because the answer must be written in the form *`open parentheses p plus q x plus r x squared close parentheses y`* and *`y equals straight e to the power of open parentheses 4 x minus x squared close parentheses end exponent`

`fraction numerator straight d squared y over denominator straight d x squared end fraction equals open square brackets negative 2 plus 4 open parentheses 2 minus x close parentheses open parentheses 2 minus x close parentheses close square brackets straight e to the power of open parentheses 4 x minus x squared close parentheses end exponent`

**[M1]**

A sphere of radius $r$ cm and volume $V$ cm<sup>3</sup>  is increasing in size with time $t$ seconds. The volume increases at a constant rate of 24 cm<sup>3</sup> s<sup>-1</sup>.

Find the exact rate at which the radius is increasing when the sphere reaches a volume of $\frac{32π}{3}$ cm<sup>3</sup>.
parts.solution_md:
> *The volume of a sphere is given in the exam*

$V=\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}$

> *This question requires connect rates of change (an application of the chain rule)*

$\frac{dV}{dt}=\frac{dV}{dr}\times\frac{dr}{dt}$

> *Find *$\frac{dV}{dr}$* by differentiating *$V=\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}$

`table row cell fraction numerator straight d V over denominator straight d r end fraction end cell equals cell 4 over 3 pi open parentheses 3 r squared close parentheses end cell row blank equals cell 4 pi r squared end cell end table`

**[B1]**

> *You know *$\frac{dV}{dt}=24$* from the question *

> *Substitute *$\frac{dV}{dt}=24$* and *`table row cell fraction numerator straight d V over denominator straight d r end fraction end cell equals cell 4 pi r squared end cell end table`* into *$\frac{dV}{dt}=\frac{dV}{dr}\times\frac{dr}{dt}$

$24=4πr^{2}\times\frac{dr}{dt}$

**[M1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> This mark is for using a correct connected rate formula, e.g.  $\frac{dV}{dt}=\frac{dV}{dr}\times\frac{dr}{dt}$ or $\frac{dr}{dt}=\frac{dr}{dV}\times\frac{dV}{dt}$, with at least one correct substitution into the formula.

> *The question wants you to find *$\frac{dr}{dt}$* so make *$\frac{dr}{dt}$* the subject*

`table row cell fraction numerator straight d r over denominator straight d t end fraction end cell equals cell fraction numerator 24 over denominator 4 pi r squared end fraction end cell row blank equals cell fraction numerator 6 over denominator pi r squared end fraction end cell end table`

> *You need the value of *$\frac{dr}{dt}$* when *$V=\frac{32π}{3}$* but *$\frac{dr}{dt}$* is in terms of *$r$* not *$V$

> *Use *$V=\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}$* to find *$r$* when *$V=\frac{32π}{3}$

`table row cell fraction numerator 32 pi over denominator 3 end fraction end cell equals cell 4 over 3 pi r cubed end cell row cell 32 pi end cell equals cell 4 pi r cubed end cell row 8 equals cell r cubed end cell row r equals 2 end table`

**[A1]**

> *Substitute *$r=2$* into *$\frac{dr}{dt}$

`table row cell fraction numerator straight d r over denominator straight d t end fraction end cell equals cell fraction numerator 6 over denominator pi open parentheses 2 close parentheses squared end fraction end cell row blank equals cell fraction numerator 6 over denominator 4 pi end fraction end cell row blank equals cell fraction numerator 3 over denominator 2 pi end fraction end cell end table`

> *The units are cm for *$r$* and seconds for *$t$*, so cm/s for *$\frac{dr}{dt}$
